description: TJX is the largest off-price apparel and home-fashion retailer, with 5,214 stores at January 31, 2026 (TJ Maxx, Marshalls, HomeGoods, Sierra, Winners, TK Maxx and others) and fiscal 2026 net sales of $60.4 billion. It does not make anything. Its buyers, more than 1,400 of them, buy brand-name goods from about 21,000 vendors at a discount (closeouts, cancelled orders, overruns, special production) and sell them in stores at prices generally 20% to 60% below full-price retailers, with no promotions or coupons. The model is opportunistic buying close to need and fast inventory turns, so the assortment is a changing 'treasure hunt'; only about 2% of Marmaxx sales are online. It earns a 15.1% segment margin in its US apparel division and about 12% in HomeGoods, and lower in Europe and Australia (7.0%).

businessLines.name: Marmaxx (TJ Maxx, Marshalls, Sierra)
businessLines.how: Retail markup: buys branded goods opportunistically at a discount and sells them in stores at 20% to 60% below full-price retailers' regular prices; profit is the gap between buy cost and shelf price, held up by fast turns and few markdowns.
businessLines.description: 2,603 TJ Maxx and Marshalls stores in the US (plus 145 Sierra stores, results included in Marmaxx) selling family apparel, footwear, accessories, beauty, jewelry and home fashions. Largest off-price retailer in the US per the 10-K.

revenue.note: Net sales; FY2025 $34,604M; Q2 FY2027 (quarter to Aug 1, 2026) $9,109M vs $8,841M

businessLines.revenueNote: Net sales; FY2025 $34,604M; Q2 FY2027 (quarter to Aug 1, 2026) $9,109M vs $8,841M

operatingProfit.note: FY2025 $4,895M; includes a net benefit from the credit card interchange fee litigation settlement; Q2 FY2027 $1,424M vs $1,254M

businessLines.name: HomeGoods (HomeGoods, Homesense)
businessLines.how: Same off-price retail markup on home goods bought as closeouts and overruns, sold in stores 20% to 60% below full-price retailers.
businessLines.description: 963 HomeGoods and 79 Homesense stores in the US selling furniture, rugs, lighting, soft home, decor, tabletop and cookware, plus pet and gourmet food; the 10-K calls HomeGoods the leading US off-price home fashions retailer.

businessLines.name: TJX Canada (Winners, HomeSense, Marshalls)
businessLines.how: Off-price retail markup in Canada; segment results are reported in US dollars.
businessLines.description: 316 Winners, 162 HomeSense and 111 Marshalls stores in Canada; Winners is the leading off-price family apparel and home fashions retailer in Canada per the 10-K.

businessLines.name: TJX International (TK Maxx, Homesense Europe, TK Maxx Australia)
businessLines.how: Off-price retail markup outside North America (UK, Ireland, Germany, Poland, Austria, Netherlands, Australia).
businessLines.description: 673 TK Maxx stores in Europe (UK, Ireland, Germany, Poland, Austria, Netherlands, and Spain from March 2026), 74 Homesense stores in the UK and Ireland, 88 TK Maxx in Australia; tkmaxx.com, tkmaxx.de and tkmaxx.at online. The 10-K calls TK Maxx Europe's largest major brick-and-mortar off-price retailer of apparel and home fashions.
